questions.q: What's the first step in the working checklist for building a complete model?
options: Sort tables into fact and dimension
Set cross filter direction on every relationship
Resolve active vs. inactive relationships
Write DAX measures
questions.explain: Before creating relationships or setting options, you first need to know which tables summarize events (fact) and which describe things (dimension).

questions.q: When reading a finished model in Model view, what should you look for first?
options: The fact table — the one every other table connects to
Which table has the most columns
Which table was created first
The table with the longest name
questions.explain: Finding the fact table at the center gives you the anchor point for reading the rest of the model's shape and relationships.

questions.q: What should you check for when a model has two fact-like tables sharing dimensions?
options: Loops, and whether cross filter direction creates ambiguity between the shared dimensions
Whether both fact tables use exactly the same column names
That one of the fact tables is deleted
That all relationships are set to many-to-many
questions.explain: Two fact tables sharing a dimension table is a classic loop shape — exactly the scenario from Lesson 29 where Both cross filter direction can create ambiguity.

questions.q: Why does a correct data model matter for the next chapter on DAX?
options: DAX measures depend entirely on relationships to know which rows to sum, count, or average
DAX doesn't use relationships at all
DAX can only be written after all data is deleted and reloaded
DAX replaces the need for relationships
questions.explain: A DAX measure written against a broken or ambiguous model will return a wrong number with no warning — the model has to be correct first.

questions.q: What's the target shape this entire chapter builds toward?
options: Star schema — one fact table at the center, dimension tables around it
A single flat table with every column combined
A chain of tables connected end to end
A model with no relationships at all
questions.explain: Every lesson in this chapter — from fact vs. dimension through active/inactive relationships — exists to help you build and maintain a correct star schema.
